GANs are a type of machine learning model that uses two neural networks to generate and create new data samples
The model is trained to take as input a random sample of data and produce a sample that looks like it was generated by the same data
The model is trained to be able to generate samples that are similar to the input data
The performance of the model is measured by its ability to generate samples that are close to the input data
The quality of the generated samples is measured by their accuracy and uniqueness
The architecture of the model is typically a combination of a generator and a discriminator
The generator is a neural network that takes as input a random sample of data and produces a new sample that looks like it was generated by the same data
The discriminator is a neural network that takes as input a new sample and tries to determine whether it is a generated sample or not
The generator is trained to be able to produce samples that are close to the discriminator's output
The discriminator is trained to be able to detect the difference between a generated sample and a real sample
The model is typically trained using a loss function that measures the difference between the generator's output and the discriminator's output
